summary_paragraph: A female patient with a history of gunshot wound to the spine resulting in paraplegia, neurogenic bladder, and chronic indwelling Foley catheter use presented after a fall from her wheelchair following alcohol intoxication. She reported new-onset lower back pain and persistent foul-smelling urine despite recent treatment with trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole for a presumed complicated urinary tract infection. Urinalysis showed nitrite positivity and many bacteria, and a urine culture later showed no growth, suggesting early response to new antibiotics. Blood cultures revealed gram-positive cocci and subsequently gram-positive rods, indicating bacteremia. She was treated with IV ceftriaxone for suspected pyelonephritis and bacteremia. Imaging showed no acute intracranial abnormalities or fractures. Despite medical advice, the patient eloped from the hospital on the morning of April 17 before completing treatment. She was discharged on oral pain medications and phenazopyridine with strong recommendations to follow up and complete antibiotic therapy.
